questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency and parking brakes must use mechanical force to hold.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.text: Should only be used if another vehicle is close.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you are signaling.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after driving a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check if rocks are in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance to make sure the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share the brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside the trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside the trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside the trailer.
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles are more likely to roll over. Keep cargo weight as low as possible in the trailer to reduce this risk.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when the road surface has poor traction. Reduce your speed by one-half or more when driving on packed snow.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block other drivers, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and slow down traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Explosives are classified as Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your bloodstream?
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed speed. Nothing can speed this up. The only way to sober up is to wait and let your body process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes cannot build up pressure?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If your brakes will not build pressure, try shifting to a lower gear. You can also pump the brakes or use the emergency brake.

questions.question: Aggressive driving means:

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with care for other drivers' safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy way without regard for other drivers' safety or rights.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a fire in your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are unsure which fire extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous fire, wait for firefighters to arrive and handle it.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency brakes will automatically activate.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on the road is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it may look like wet pavement. Be very careful when it is cold and the road looks wet.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Is probably aware of their surroundings.
May not be aware of their surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not be aware of their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians and joggers wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle coming and could step into traffic without knowing you are there.

questions.question: When visibility is poor and you are driving near other vehicles, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when visibility is poor and you are driving near others. Use low beams at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather. High beams can blind other drivers.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, you should:

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes to the report.
Review the report first when inspecting the vehicle.
Skip your own inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the report first when inspecting the vehicle.
questions.explanation: As your first step, review any inspection report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to:

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection. You must tell the examiner what you are checking and explain why each part is important.
